page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This hardware profile does not include any integrated GPUs or local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage.

The arm64 architecture of the c4a-standard-32 requires software workloads to be compiled specifically for ARM, which represents a key compatibility consideration compared to x86-based instances. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource contention from neighboring tenants. However, the lack of local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses means users must factor in additional network and storage resources when configuring this instance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture typically offers a favorable resource-to-cost ratio for multi-threaded workloads that do not require specialized x86 instruction sets or hardware acceleration. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance appropriate for general-purpose workloads, web serving, containerized microservices, and distributed application nodes that benefit from dedicated processing cores and moderate memory density.
